subject.title: [security] Local Actions setup-node trusts an unverified Node.js archive as a workflow binary

question: What integrity control should local `actions/setup-node` hydration enforce before installing or reusing a downloaded Node archive?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing the trust root, fail-closed behavior, and cache invalidation marker defines a security boundary and may affect existing local hydration workflows.

options.title: Verify release SHASUMS before install
options.body: Fetch the selected version's published SHA-256 metadata, require an archive-name match, verify before extraction, mark cache entries by digest, and fail closed on missing or mismatched integrity data.

options.title: Disable local setup-node downloads
options.body: Require a preinstalled compatible Node or `--github-runner` until maintainers approve a stronger signed-metadata design, preserving safety at the cost of local hydration coverage.

options.title: Keep HTTPS-only behavior
options.body: Treat this as defense-in-depth and leave the current download path unchanged, accepting that documented local setup-node hydration trusts a network archive without a release integrity check.

recommendation.title: Verify release SHASUMS before install
recommendation.body: Fetch the selected version's published SHA-256 metadata, require an archive-name match, verify before extraction, mark cache entries by digest, and fail closed on missing or mismatched integrity data.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced local Actions hydration and authored the security-boundary documentation that determines whether this path must fail closed.
